title: The street and the law
theme: Muggings, lurkers and police seen from the edges: a victim afterward, a witness, someone avoiding the station, a lurker with a day job.

storylets.title: An officer on the beat
storylets.note: Plain presence. People look away, or do not.

b1: {B.desc} strolls the block, hands clasped behind {B.his} back, eyes on the doors.
{B.desc} makes a slow circuit of the block, a scanner on {B.his} belt.
{B.desc} walks the beat, boots loud on stone, stopping at every corner.
{B.desc} patrols the sidewalk under the flickering signs.
b2: {A} crosses to the other side as the officer approaches.
{A} walks on at the same pace and does not turn {A.his} head.
{A} nods once at {B.desc} and keeps going.
{A} steps around {B.desc}, eyes on the ground.

storylets.title: A scan at the corner
storylets.note: A routine scanner check. Nothing comes of it most of the time.

B.desc: a patrol officer with a scanner

b1: {B.desc} raises a scanner toward {A} and holds it steady.
{B.desc} sweeps the scanner over {A.his} wrist and checks the readout.
{B.desc} stops {A} at the corner and runs the scanner down {A.his} front.
b2: {A} holds still, both arms out from {A.his} sides.
{A} stands under the lamp while the scanner blinks.
{A} stays at the corner, jaw tight, eyes on the officer's boots.
b3: {B.desc} waves {A} on. {A} walks off, rolling {A.his} shoulders.
{A} is let go and heads down the block, not quite hurrying.
{A} walks away fast, one fist shoved in a pocket.

storylets.title: The long way around the station
storylets.note: Someone changes course to avoid the police station door. Observed only; no reason is stated.

b1: {A} walks along the block toward the station, head down.
{A} approaches the corner by the station, collar turned up.
{A} heads up the sidewalk toward the station door.
b2: {A} stops a pace short of the station's lights and stands there.
{A} halts and looks at the door, then at the street.
{A} stays at the corner for a moment, hands in {A.his} pockets.
b3: {A} crosses to the far side and takes the long way around.
{A} turns off into a side street and speeds up.
{A} goes back the way {A.he} came.

log: {A} crosses away from the station door again: {seen} days on the feed.
{A} turns away a few paces short of the station door, at the same corner: {seen} days now.

storylets.title: A few words at the station door
storylets.note: A person speaks to an officer. The watcher hears only what is said aloud.

B.desc: an officer at the station door

b1: {A} comes up to the station door and stops short of it.
{A} approaches the station with a slip of paper and a pinched look.
{A} arrives at the station and waits at the bay.
b2: {B.desc} listens, tablet out, and nods. {A} talks with both hands.
{A} speaks and {B.desc} types it into a tablet.
{B.desc} asks a short question. {A} answers slowly.
b3: {A} hands back a stylus and walks away from the station.
{A} steps away from the station door, folding a receipt.
{A} leaves the step and crosses the street.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "I saw a man go through the back door of the shop at about nine. Short, gray jacket."
Overheard: {A} says: "No, I did not see his face. I saw the jacket and the limp."

storylets.title: Sitting very still on a bench
storylets.note: The robbery happened off screen. The watcher sees only the aftermath, then hears of it secondhand.

A.desc: an adult on a bench, empty hands

b1: {A} sits very still on a bench with both hands open on {A.his} knees.
{A} perches on the bench, jacket askew, staring at the pavers.
{A} takes a seat with a pale, flat face and does not move.
b2: {B.desc} comes over and holds out a cup of water. {A} takes it.
{B.desc} passes {A} a bottle and says a few words.
{B.desc} hands {A} a folded handkerchief.
b3: {A} takes a call on a borrowed comm, voice low and shaky.
{A} lifts a comm to one ear and gives short, flat answers.
{A} takes a comm call and answers in broken pieces.

log: Comm, one side: {A} says: "Everything. The card, the keys. It was a man with a hood."
Comm, one side: {A} says: "No, I'm fine. They only wanted the bag. I'll call the station."

lines: Overheard: {S} says to {L} that {A.desc} was mugged by the metro the other day. Bag and everything.
Overheard: {S} tells {L}: "Did you hear? {A.desc} got robbed on the way home. Lucky no one was hurt."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} lost {A.his} bag in a holdup and has been jumpy ever since.
Overheard: {S} mentions to {L} that {A.desc} was robbed near the stalls.
entry: Was robbed on the way home, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Lost a bag in a holdup, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Was held up near the metro, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: Hands up in the passage
storylets.note: A real mugging seen live. Rare, brief, no gore. Chain: law.after-robbery as hearsay follow-up.

b1: A hooded figure steps out of a side street toward {A}.
{B.desc} darts out of an alley mouth and closes on {A}.
{B.desc} cuts across the street and blocks {A.his} path.
b2: {A} freezes with both hands half raised. A bag changes hands.
{A} stands frozen while {B.desc} pulls at the strap of {A.his} bag.
{A} holds still. The bag is gone from {A.his} shoulder.
b3: {B.desc} flees into the dark, the bag clutched to {B.his} chest.
{B.desc} melts into the alley and is gone.
{B.desc} vanishes down a side street at a dead run.

storylets.title: Taken in at the corner
storylets.note: An arrest seen live. Rare. The reason is never stated; the player sees only the action.

b1: A patrol bike drops in beside {A} at the curb. {B.desc} swings off.
{B.desc} arrives on a police bike and steps in front of {A}.
{B.desc} lands the bike across {A.his} path.
b2: {A} raises both hands. {B.desc} cuffs {A.his} wrists in front.
{A} stands still while {B.desc} scans {A.him}, then holds out both wrists.
{B.desc} cuffs {A} and steers {A.him} onto the back of the bike.
b3: The bike lifts away with both of them.
{B.desc} and {A} leave the corner on the bike.
The police bike hums off toward the station.

storylets.title: A figure at the same corner
storylets.note: Someone stands at a corner every night. The watcher can learn who they are by day. Chain: law.lurker-at-work.

A.desc: an adult standing at a dark corner

b1: {A} stands at a dark corner, {A.his} hood half up, motionless.
{A} stays under a dead lamp, one shoulder against the wall.
{A} lingers at the corner and watches the crowd go by.
b2: {A} waves at a passing drone, then lowers {A.his} hand.
{A} lifts a hand to someone across the street.
{A} waves at the empty sidewalk and puts {A.his} hand back in a pocket.
b3: {A} walks off along the wall, unhurried.
{A} leaves the corner and heads into a side street.
{A} moves on at an even pace.

storylets.title: The same face behind a counter
storylets.note: By day the corner figure works a counter. Learned through a name badge, which is verified.

b1: {A} works the counter, apron on, ladling broth into bowls.
{A} serves a line of customers without looking up.
{A} stacks cups at the stall and calls an order over {A.his} shoulder.
{A} sets a bowl down and wipes the counter in one move.
b2: {A} stands at the edge of the stall and yawns into a sleeve.
{A} leans on the counter during a lull, eyes half closed.
{A} stays at the back of the stall, arms folded.
{A} stands by the register and counts coins into a tin.

log: A name badge pinned to {A.his} front reads {A.first}, Counter Staff.
A patch on {A.his} sleeve reads Counter Crew.

storylets.title: Handed back, nothing missing
storylets.note: Someone finds a dropped wallet and chases the owner down.

A.desc: an adult who picked up a wallet

b1: {A} spots a flat leather wallet on the sidewalk and picks it up.
{A} stoops, pulls a wallet from the edge of a puddle, and wipes it on a sleeve.
{A} scoops a wallet from the curb and looks around.
b2: {A} runs down the block after a figure, wallet held up.
{A} sprints after someone, shouting and waving the wallet.
{A} jogs through the crowd, calling out.
b3: {A} catches up and hands the wallet to {B.desc}. {B.desc} opens it and stares.
{A} holds out the wallet and {B.desc} takes it with both hands.
{A} presses the wallet into the hand of {B.desc}.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "I'm {B.first}. Thank you. Everything I own is in there."
Overheard: {A} says: "The card inside says {B.first}. That's you? Be careful next time."

storylets.title: A friendly word about the hour
storylets.note: A patrol officer tells someone to head home. Nothing is enforced.

b1: {A} lounges on a bench with a cup, the seats around {A.him} empty.
{A} sits on a bench in the dark, {A.his} feet up on the slats.
{A} takes a bench seat and watches the lamps.
b2: {B.desc} stops by the bench and says a few words about the hour. {A} answers politely.
{A} and {B.desc} talk. {B.desc} points toward the nearest metro.
{B.desc} asks {A} something and nods at the reply.
b3: {A} gets up and walks off down the street.
{A} stands, stretches, and leaves the bench.
{A} leaves, tossing a salute over {A.his} shoulder.
